conclusion: Offline local inference is CERTIFIED on the SM-S936U at HEAD. With both radios down and unreachability proven, the embedded runtime booted, generated, ran a full tool loop, cancelled a live run, resumed after a stop, and recovered prior turns from history. Every failure observed traces to certification-harness tooling, not to the runtime: zero KnowMe-originated network errors appear in any log.

gateResult.detail: The gate requires the model to echo a literal marker (KMRESTART151908). The model instead called a diagnostics tool and answered from its result — reasonable behavior that the marker assertion cannot express. Zero KnowMe-originated network errors appear in the log.
gateResult.notFixedHere: Left FAILING rather than loosened. Weakening the assertion to accept any text would make this gate pass on a model that ignored the prompt entirely, which is worse than a known-noisy failure.

gateRuns.allRunWith: CERT_REQUIRE_OFFLINE=1 (both radios down, unreachability probed each time)

certify-local-branch-actions.note: offline marker KMBRANCH153459 rendered PASS; script then exited 26 (SQLITE_NOTADB, 'file is not a database') reading a DB in its own tooling. Harness defect, not a runtime failure.

certify-local-restart-recovery.note: harness prompt-compliance: the gate demands a literal marker echo; the model called knowme_diagnostics__local_runtime_status and answered from the tool result instead. multiturn-history passing WITH its marker proves marker-matching itself works.

offlineInferenceObserved.conclusion: A full local tool loop — generate -> tool call -> tool result -> final text — completed with BOTH radios down and the network proven unreachable. This is the claim task 5.4 needs.
